claims.content: The use case allows the User to compress one or more objects (files or archives) in one or more compressed archive volumes in one of the formats offered for compression by PeaZip.

goal.raw_text: The use case allows the User to compress one or more objects (files or archives) in one or more compressed archive volumes in one of the formats offered for compression by PeaZip.

claims.content: User
PeaZip is available as a file and archive manager application for a computer system that allows users to compress/decompress, authenticate and archive them.
The User has access to the Create Archive Interface.
One or more objects (files or archives) are to be included in the compressed archive.
The archive format is not a read-only supported format.
The User initiates the use case by opening the Create archive window (Create archive Interface).

trigger.raw_text: The User initiates the use case by opening the Create archive window (Create archive Interface).

claims.content: In the Create archive window (Create archive Interface), the User selects the compression format from a list of the supported by PeaZip formats for archiving and compression for the created archive.
The Create archive Interface presents a configuration dialog for creating a new, empty ZIP archive with optional formatting and security settings, awaiting user input to proceed.
The User provides input to proceed with the archive creation job.
A modal dialog box is overlaid, indicating completion of an archive creation job, with the title bar reading “Done: Create peazip_portable-2.5.WIN64-1.zip”.
Under the Status tab, the text states “Job successfully completed”.
Alternative path from main flow step 0: The User can approach the Create archive window (Create archive Interface) through 'Go to archiving layout', which leads directly to create archive interface.
Alternative path from main flow step 2: The Create Archive Interface receives input from the 'Drag and Drop Feature' for providing input to proceed.

Alternative path from main flow step 2: The User can choose storage space (in the computer system) where the archive is going to be saved and set archive's name, as well as define what should happen in case of existence of a homonym file or archive in the selected storage space.
Alternative path from main flow step 2: The User can split selected objects' data content and compress it into more than one archive volumes, with the size of each of them defined by user.
Alternative path from main flow step 2: The User can append timestamp to the created archive's name for archiving and backup purpose.
Alternative path from main flow step 2: The User can encrypt ('lock') the created archives by setting password and (optionally) keyfile.
1. If the selected compression format is a read-only supported format, compression to read-only supported formats is not possible; the use case exits without creating the compressed archive.
The archive creation job is successfully completed, as indicated by the modal dialog's Status tab stating “Job successfully completed”.
One or more objects (files or archives) are compressed in one or more compressed archive volumes in one of the offered for compression by PeaZip formats.
The compressed archive volume(s) are sizing less or equally to the original ones.
The created archive’s name and storage space (in the computer system) are defined by the User.

If the User chose to split selected objects’ data content, the selected objects’ data content is split and compressed into more than one archive volumes, with the size of each of them defined by the User.
If a timestamp was appended, the timestamp is appended to the created archive’s name for archiving and backup purpose.
If encryption (“locking”) was used, a password and (optionally) a keyfile are set to the created archives.

The objects that are contained in the created archive are not destroyed, are not deleted and are not left empty; they retain their content and name and remain saved at the same space of the computer system where they were initially stored.
